newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX PV electricity seen opening higher, COB flat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX PV electricity seen opening higher, COB flat.

text.p: NYMEX Palo Verde (PV) electricity futures were called to open higher Monday on very hot weather in the interior part of the Southwest, while California-Oregon Border (COB) was seen flat on mild weather.
The complex ended lower Friday on easing physical prices and restarts of several large western generating units.
"It tried to rally this morning but it didn't go very far," a Houston futures trader said.
Brokers and traders said PV futures rose in early over-the-counter (OTC) trading on light volume.
"There's very little trading. People are holding on for more San Onofre news," another trader said.

The 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear station in southern California reached hot shutdown status, which means the reactor is active but not putting power on the grid, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said.
The adjacent 1,080 MW San Onofre unit 3 was scheduled to restart Thursday.
Meanwhile, OTC prices were showing signs of waning.
August Palo Verde (PV) deliveries in OTC activity were talked at $35.75-36.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) up from Friday's settlement at $35,27 after traded as high as $36.10.
August California-Oregon Border (COB) was quoted at $22.40-22.60 above Monday's close at $22.68 after talking as high as $22.90.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was operating at 42 percent power early Monday and set to hit full power midweek after repairs.
The Washington Public Power Supply System unit took WNP-2 off line last Thursday to correct a cooling system problem.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was shut Friday for three weeks for repairs.
Moreover, the 750 MW unit 1 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Ariz., was said to shut Friday until this morning for repairs.
A 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming tripped off line Friday and was scheduled to resume operation today.

Moreover, the 750 MW unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant was tentatively set to restart Friday today after its startup was postponed from Wednesday. The unit in Nevada tripped off a week ago due to a boiler tube leak.

The Pacific Northwest was expected to see readings rising to one to five degrees F above normal with chance of showers midweek, while the Southwest would continue to experience dry and seasonal hot weather.

Coastal cities from Seattle to San Diego were predicted to see temperatures in the 70s-80s and interior centers like Phoenix and Las Vegas are forecast to feel heat in the 106-111 degree range, according to Weather Services Corp.
